name: MASTER OF BIT MANIPULATION
title: Grandmaster Ragine, Keeper of the Thirty-Two

placeholders.days: whole days since the relevant event — the student's last visit, a past failure, or the length of the current practice streak
placeholders.streak: number of consecutive correct drills in the current run
placeholders.attempts: how many attempts the student previously needed on this problem
placeholders.requirement: name of the gate dimension that is short: recognition, understanding, implementation, or retention
placeholders.shortfall: how far the short gate dimension sits below its threshold, as a percentage

greeting_first: You are here for the bits. Sit.
Decimal is a courtesy the machine extends to you. Here we return it.
Everything you have written until now, something translated for you. I teach you to stop needing a translator.
You count in tens because you have ten fingers. The machine has two states. We will speak to it in its own language.
greeting_returning: Sit. We continue where we stopped.
greeting_after_gap: {days} days. The bits did not move. You did.
You were away {days} days. Nothing here changed. We start one step back.
Gone {days} days. Recall decays faster than skill. Today I test both.
{days} days is long enough to forget. Not long enough to be sorry for. Begin.
lesson_intro: Before you fight, understand your weapon.
One observation. It will collapse a class of problems.
Watch. Then do it without me.
This is a small thing. Small things carry the weight here.
lesson_memorise: Memorise it. You will use it often.
This one you keep. Not in notes — in the hand.
Learn it until you no longer read it.
You will not have time to derive this later. Take it now.
drill_wrong: That is not the answer. Read the mask again.
No. You shifted before you masked. The order matters.
Wrong. The bit you cleared was not the lowest set bit.
That holds for positive n only. Try it again with n negative.
Not that. Write the number in binary first, then answer.
drill_streak: {streak} in a row. The hand is beginning to move without you. Continue.
That is fluency starting. Do not slow down now.
trial_intro: I name nothing now. Read it and decide.
No label. Find the technique yourself.
From here you are alone with the problem. Begin.
The signals are in the constraints. They always were.
fail_wrong_pattern: Wrong technique. Reread the constraints — they named the right one.
You reached for the wrong weapon. The size of the state space told you what to use. Look again.
Not that one. Ask first what the input is small enough to allow, then choose.
The approach cannot work here at any speed. Back to the signals. We read them together.
fail_timeout: Time. You had it and could not reach it.
Time. You knew the technique. You were slow to trust it.
Time ran out. That is a fluency problem, not a knowledge problem. We drill it away.
Time. Nothing you did was wrong. It was only late. Again.
fail_wrong_answer: Right technique. Wrong implementation. Check the shift width.
The approach held. The code did not. Test it at n = 0.
You chose correctly and executed badly. That is the easier failure to repair. Again.
Correct idea, broken edge. The highest bit betrayed you.
Off by one bit is still off. Trace it by hand, then resubmit.
success: Done. The next one is harder.
success_fast: No hesitation. That is what the drills were for.
praise_exceptional: That was well done. You saw the trap before it appeared.
Clean, fast, and correct at the edges. Few reach that on this pattern.
That is the best you have done here. You did not guess — you knew.
You solved the problem the machine was actually asking. That is rarer than speed.
praise_major: I have trained many students. Few remain when the problems become difficult. You did. You have earned my respect.
You arrived thinking in tens. You think in twos now, and you did not stop when it stopped being new. I have little to give. Take this: you have earned my respect.
Talent arrives loudly and leaves quietly. You did neither. You returned, you worked, and the machine's own language answers to you now. You have earned my respect.
memorisation_detected: You remember the solution. You do not understand the technique. That is not mastery. I will give you a different problem.
You recall the shape of an answer you have seen. Change the skin and you are lost. We go back one step.
The problems you have met, you pass. The fresh ones, you fail. That gap is memory, not skill. Another problem.
improvement_noticed: You failed this {days} days ago. Today you solved it. That is improvement. Continue.
This was your weakness. It is not any more. I noticed.
You needed {attempts} attempts once. Today, one. Good.
The thing that stopped you does not stop you now. Remember that the next time something does.
commitment_noticed: {days} days in a row. Most stop before now. You did not.
You keep returning. That is the one thing I cannot teach.
Talent is common. Attendance is not. Continue.
You have come back after every failure so far. I am counting.
gate_locked: Not yet. {requirement} is short by {shortfall} percent. Return when it is not.
The gate holds. Your recognition is short — you know the tricks, you do not yet see when to use them.
No. Understanding is short. You can write it. You cannot explain it. Those are different.
Implementation is short. The idea is sound and the code is not. Drill, then come back.
Retention is short. What you learned last week you have already dropped. Review first.
gate_open: The gate is open. Come when you are ready.
You meet the requirements. The final test waits.
Enough. You may attempt it now.
Nothing is short any more. The rest is yours to decide.
final_test_intro: I will not tell you what technique to use.
I will not tell you what technique to use. That was the point of every drill before this.
Three problems. Nothing named. Decide for yourself.
No help from me now. Only what you carry.
victory: It is done. You read the machine's own language now.
You passed. The bits hold nothing further that I can teach you.
Finished. Carry it out with you — the next master will assume you have it.
That is mastery. Not speed, not memory. Mastery. Go.
